meta.purpose: c2r-hoist-a BASE fixture — agent-visible OpenAI tool payloads of the six cohort-A factories, captured PRE-HOIST from the SECOND (warm) build of each factory.
meta.invariant: After hoisting the factory-local input models to module level, the warm-build payloads MUST be byte-identical to these entries (json.dumps equality, exact key order, no sort_keys).

function.name: job_create
function.description:
Submit a new job to the queue. Use tool_help("job_create") for details.

queue_id accepts a queue ID or a system-queue alias (e.g. "parallel"
= system_parallel_queue; case-insensitive). When omitted: ari/jober
target system_parallel_queue by default; other agents get the
service default (FIFO for task jobs).

agent_id.description: Agent ID to run the job (e.g., 'developer', 'leader')

project_id.description: Project ID for isolation and routing

queue_id.description: Queue to submit to: a queue ID or a system-queue alias (system_fifo_queue|fifo, system_parallel_queue|parallel, system_background_queue|background, system_defer_queue|defer, system_kb_fifo_queue|kb_fifo; case-insensitive). Omit to use your agent default (ari/jober: system_parallel_queue) or the service default (FIFO).

source.description: DEPRECATED and IGNORED (NIT-7, P2.3 review cycle 1): the server derives source UNCONDITIONALLY since B3.5 (agent:<caller> for agent callers, internal_agent:unknown otherwise) — any value passed here has no effect. Param retained purely for schema compat; removal deferred.

watch.description: Watch the job for lifecycle events. Default: True (FP4-PP2 2026-10-03 user-approved flip — agent-lane auto-watches so completions are never lost). Explicit watch=False still wins.

function.name: job_get
function.description: Get job details by ID. Use tool_help("job_get") for details.

function.name: job_list
function.description:
List jobs with optional filters. Use tool_help("job_list") for details.

``status`` answers the transport question ("was my submission
handled?"). For the outcome question ("is the work done?"),
use the mission tools (``get_mission`` / ``await_mission``).
The ``mission_ref`` cross-reference on every terminal job
payload ties the two layers together in a single read.

statuses.description: Filter by job status. Valid values: pending, processing, completed, failed, cancelled, dead_letter. Aliases accepted: running (=processing), done (=completed), error (=failed), waiting (=pending). Case-insensitive.

job_types.description: M2 (mission-class, 2026-09-02): optional JobItem.job_type filter — accepted values are ``task`` and ``message``. Default: BOTH kinds. Additive vs the legacy ``statuses`` filter, which is RETAINED through the M3 window (contract draft §4). On the resolver path the filter is applied client-side (the resolver's ``list_work`` does not narrow by job_type today).

function.name: watch_job
function.description:
Watch a job for lifecycle events. If the job is already in a terminal state, immediate notification is attempted (the reply reflects the held/delivered split — see F-2 fixback).

Use tool_help("watch_job") for details.

events.description: Specific events to watch for (default: all terminal states + in_progress). M2 (mission-class): the value ``mission_terminal`` is OPT-IN — when included, the watcher fires ONLY when admission AND mission liveness are BOTH terminal (contract draft §3.5). Default watchers (without ``mission_terminal``) keep transport-only semantics — back-compat preserved.

function.name: unwatch_job
function.description:
Stop watching a job for lifecycle events.

The handle is tolerant (toolset reshape 2026-09-19, design §7):
it may be a receipt job_id OR a mission_id — a mission handle
resolves to every watched receipt of that mission and removes
them all.

Use tool_help("unwatch_job") for details.

job_id.description: The job ID to stop watching

function.name: list_watched_jobs
function.description:
List all jobs the current instance is watching.

Rows are labeled by resolving their handles (toolset reshape
2026-09-19, design §7): ``mission handle`` (the row keys on a
mission id), ``receipt of mission <id>`` (a receipt-keyed row
and the mission it belongs to), or unlabeled (unresolvable
receipt).

Use tool_help("list_watched_jobs") for details.

function.name: watch_jobs
function.description:
Watch multiple jobs for lifecycle events. Bulk version of watch_job.

Use tool_help("watch_jobs") for details.

job_ids.description: List of job IDs to watch

events.description: Specific events to watch for (default: all terminal states + in_progress). M2 (mission-class): the value ``mission_terminal`` is OPT-IN — same semantics as ``watch_job`` (contract draft §3.5).

function.name: job_answer
function.description:
Submit the orchestrator's answer to a pending question pack on a watched job.

Use tool_help("job_answer") for details.

work_id.description: The work_id whose instance asked the question (matches the work_id on the ``[JOB_EVENT] Job ... question requested ❓`` line that the watcher received — the question event is mission-scoped, so this may be any receipt of the asking mission; resolution to the asker is watcher-independent).

answers.description: User-supplied answers. Key by question id (the id carried in the pending pack payload) — text-keyed fallbacks are also accepted by the helper.

question_pack_id.description: The pack id from the pending question payload (``question_pack.id`` echoed in the ``[JOB_EVENT]`` body). Mandatory for the T1″ stale-answers hijack guard; a mismatch is rejected with ``QUESTION_PACK_MISMATCH``.

function.name: job_pause
function.description: Pause the instance behind an ACTIVE job and cascade to its lineage. Use tool_help("job_pause") for details.

job_id.description: The work_id of an ACTIVE (non-terminal, instance-bearing) job to pause. Its whole instance lineage pauses with it.

function.name: job_resume
function.description: Resume the instance behind a PAUSED job and cascade to its lineage. Use tool_help("job_resume") for details.

job_id.description: The work_id of an ACTIVE job whose instance is paused. Its whole instance lineage resumes with it.

function.name: watch_mission
function.description:
Watch a MISSION (not a receipt) and be revived at mission-terminal.

Accepts a mission_id or the job_id receipt returned by
job_create / job_continue, and arms one watcher row per
currently-live receipt (already-settled receipts are skipped —
no replay of historical receipts). Mid-flight QA events
(``question requested ❓`` / ``stuck awaiting answer ⏳`` /
escalation) are MISSION-SCOPED at emission time and
events-filter-exempt: armed rows receive them even
``mission_terminal``-only — but TERMINAL coverage stays
per-receipt delta-arm (receipts minted after this call need a
re-call).

Use tool_help("watch_mission") for details.

target.description: What to watch: a mission_id (= instance_id) OR a job reference — the job_id receipt returned by job_create / job_continue. The receipt form works even before the mission is dispatched.

events.description: Watch events. Default (recommended): ['mission_terminal'] — the watch fires ONLY when admission AND mission liveness are both terminal (HOLD semantics). Explicit transport event names are accepted for advanced use.

status.description: todo | in_progress | blocked | done | 'open' (= todo|in_progress|blocked) | omit for all

due_before.description: Only items due strictly before this tz-aware ISO-8601 instant. Any UTC offset is accepted; the service normalises it to UTC before the comparison — a raw string never reaches the query.

function.name: board_link
function.description:
Mint (or regenerate) the passcode-gated public link for the board.

The board at ``/views/public/board/index.html`` is rendered FRESH
FROM THE DATABASE on every request — it always shows the current
rows, never a stale snapshot. This tool mints the ONE passcode
row that authorises reading it.

Args:
    refresh: Issue a NEW passcode. The generation is bumped, every
        outstanding grant cookie is revoked, and a lockout is
        cleared. This is the only recovery path after 10 wrong
        attempts. The default (``False``) is IDEMPOTENT — the same
        passcode and generation come back.

Returns:
    The five-line labeled shape::

        Public URL: /views/public/board/index.html
        Passcode: 7KQ2ZM
        Authenticated URL: /views/board/index.html
        Generation: 1
        Locked: no

    The ``Authenticated URL`` line is INFORMATIONAL — the direct
    lane 404s by design (the board is a DB-rendered public
    surface). On any rejection, a typed ``"Error: ..."`` string.

refresh.description: Issue a NEW passcode: bump the generation (revoking every outstanding grant cookie) and clear a lockout. This is the only recovery path after 10 wrong attempts.

project_id.description: Project ID for job routing and list filtering

function.description: List scheduled tasks (cancelled hidden by default). Use tool_help("task_schedule_list") for details.

function.name: task_schedule_cancel
function.description: Cancel a scheduled task (TERMINAL — history is preserved). Use tool_help("task_schedule_cancel") for details.

label.description: Schedule label — alternative to source_id (exact match; first match wins on collision)

function.name: task_schedule_update
function.description: Update a scheduled task (reschedule / re-message / pause / resume). Use tool_help("task_schedule_update") for details.

when.description: New trigger time (ISO 8601 for once; 'HH:MM' for daily/weekly)

timezone.description: IANA timezone; re-interprets wall-clock times in this timezone

paused.description: true = pause (resumable; a schedule left paused past the configured retention window (default 14d) is garbage-collected — history archived, config removed; resume before then is untouched. To protect a paused schedule, raise SERVICES_SOURCES_GC_TERMINAL_RETENTION_DAYS; recovery after a reap is manual, from the archive.); false = resume

function.name: view_write
function.description:
Publish an HTML page as a passcode-gated public link.

Writes ONE HTML document under the daemon-global ``reports``
root and returns the PUBLIC URL + the 6-char passcode in a
single call. The customer opens the public URL, enters the
passcode, and sees the page.

Args:
    path: Relative path under the ``reports`` root. ``.html`` is
        appended when the path carries no extension; any other
        extension is refused.
    html: The full HTML document. Served byte-for-byte — the
        tool never wraps, mutates or sanitises it.
    title: Human label (1-200 chars). Echoed only.
    overwrite: Replace an existing page. Without it, an
        existing path is an error and the original bytes stay.
    refresh: Bump the passcode generation — new code, outstanding
        grants revoked. The lockout-recovery path.

Returns:
    A stable labeled-line string: ``Public URL`` / ``Passcode``
    / ``Authenticated URL`` / ``Generation`` / ``Locked`` (the
    five ``view_link``-compatible lines) followed by ``Title`` /
    ``Bytes`` / ``Overwrote``. On any rejection, a typed
    ``"Error: ..."`` string — never a partial URL, never a
    crash.

path.description: Relative path under the reports root, e.g. '2026-10-19/board.html'. '.html' is appended when the path carries no extension. No leading '/', no '..' segments, no backslashes, no control characters.

html.description: The full HTML document (UTF-8). Served byte-for-byte; never mutated, never wrapped.

title.description: Human label (1-200 chars). Echoed in the result; NOT persisted and NOT injected into the HTML.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing page. Without it, an existing path is an error. An overwrite does NOT change the passcode or the URL.

refresh.description: Bump the passcode generation (new code, revokes outstanding grants). This is the lockout-recovery path.
